findings.description: encodeCroppedImage() outputs PNG only for image/png input; all other formats (WebP, AVIF, GIF, TIFF, BMP, ICO) become JPEG. This loses transparency (WebP/GIF) and may reduce quality (AVIF/TIFF). Documented in analyze.ts comment and tested in crop-stress.test.ts. Acceptable for vision analysis use case where JPEG is universally supported by providers.

downloadImageFromUrl() returns null for all failure modes (network error, timeout, non-2xx, size limit, no body). Caller maps this to generic 'unreadable' reason. Loses error detail but consistent with existing local-file error handling pattern. Could be enhanced later with more specific reasons.

maxRetries=1 and exponential backoff (1s) are hardcoded in analyzeImagesWithModel(). No environment variable override (VP_MAX_RETRIES, VP_RETRY_BASE_DELAY). Could be added as follow-up if users need tuning. Current defaults are reasonable for transient API errors.

testing_summary: All new tests exercise behavioral code paths via stubbed dependencies (fetch, generateTextImpl) and real image fixtures. No source-inspection-only assertions. Crop stress tests cover boundary matrices, all named regions, all supported formats, malformed inputs, and end-to-end runAnalyze integration. URL download tests stub fetch to exercise content-type parsing, size limits, and content sniffing. Transient retry tests inject flaky generateTextImpl to validate actual retry loop.
risk_rationale: Previously identified risks (invalid argument retry, inconsistent boolean parsing, hardcoded timeout) are fixed. New features (URL support, content sniffing, strict MIME, sharp crop pipeline, transient retry) are well-bounded, thoroughly tested, and follow existing patterns. No critical defects remain.
